title: Epoched versioning, rollback pathways, and cross-functional comms playbook for model-route changes
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Create an operational playbook that defines epoch-based versioning for model routes, prescriptive rollback pathways, migration guidance for integrators, and a cross-functional communications cadence to minimize customer disruption during model and API version transitions.
objectives: Define 'epoch' semantics for model routes and API compatibility guarantees
Establish deterministic rollback triggers and automated rollback tooling requirements
Create developer-facing migration guides and SDK compatibility notes
Coordinate release notes and customer comms with Sales, Support, and DevRel
Provide acceptance criteria and testing checks for gradual rollouts and canary failures
out_of_scope: Full re-architecting of model storage or model naming conventions
Long-term deprecation policy for major runtime architecture changes (handled in separate initiative)
acceptance_criteria: Epoch definition documented and approved by Eng + Research
Rollback playbook documented with concrete runbooks and example CLI commands
Migration guide published with sample SDK diffs and automated test suite examples
Release notes template and comms timeline agreed with GTM and Support
Smoke tests and canary failure thresholds codified and implemented in CI gating
deliverables: Developer migration guide (code snippets for Python/JS/REST)
Release notes template and coordinated comms schedule
Canary test matrix and CI gating changes
milestones: 2026-03-19: Draft rollback runbook and CLI examples
2026-03-26: Publish migration guide draft to docs site

2026-04-09: Final sign-off and release notes staging
2026-04-15: Target publication date and rollout start
rollout_schedule: Phase 0 (internal): 2026-04-15 to 2026-04-20 — internal-only rollout to dev/test orgs, exercise rollback paths
Phase 1 (pilot): 2026-04-21 to 2026-05-05 — invite-only customers and partner integrations, tight SLO monitoring
Phase 2 (gradual): 2026-05-06 to 2026-05-20 — percentage-based traffic ramp, automated canary checks
Phase 3 (general): 2026-05-21 — full traffic switch and broad customer communications
rollback_triggers: Sustained latency regression > 30% vs baseline for 10+ minutes
Error rate increase > 2x baseline with > 100 errors/min
Incorrectness signals from quality evaluation (regression on golden prompts)
Customer-reported critical failures for paid integrations
rollback_steps: Step 1: Pause rollout and halt traffic expansion via routing policy
Step 2: Re-route affected routes to previous epoch variant using routing API (examples in runbook)
Step 3: Execute validation smoke tests against rolled-back epoch
Step 4: Open postmortem channel and notify GTM/Support within 15 minutes
Step 5: If rollback stable for 30 minutes, create follow-up task to remediate and schedule re-release
release_notes_template: Impact: Who is affected and compatibility guarantees
Action: Required actions for integrators (code snippets)
Rollout: Phase schedule and monitoring windows
Fallback: How to roll back and who to contact

Week -2: Early-access invite to selected customers and partners
Week -1: Draft external release notes + knowledge base articles, training for Support
Go-live: Publish release notes, changelog entry, and email to affected customers
Post-launch Day 0-7: Daily status updates to internal channel and follow-up FAQs

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected model-quality regressions — Mitigation: gate by quality evals and golden prompt suite
Risk: Customers miss migration steps — Mitigation: provide one-click SDK compatibility layer and migration scripts
Risk: Rollback automation fails — Mitigation: manual rollback checklist and on-call engineering for 24h post-rollout
Risk: Misaligned comms across teams — Mitigation: single source of truth doc and daily sync during launch week
testing_and_validation: Golden prompt regression suite with pre/post diff metrics
Latency and tail-latency synthetic load tests matching production percentiles
End-to-end integration tests for SDKs and routable model variants
Canary monitor with automated rollback hook and alerting thresholds
support_playbook: Priority triage matrix for customer impact levels
Pre-written support templates for common migration questions
Escalation path: Support -> On-call runtime eng -> PM -> CTO
SLA expectations for pilot customers and enterprise tenants
notes: This playbook intentionally separates epoch semantics (compatibility guarantees) from long-term deprecation policy. The goal is to enable fast, auditable rollouts with clear rollback paths so product teams can iterate without risking customer outages.
next_steps: Produce SDK migration snippets and open PRs for docs
Schedule GTM rehearsal and tabletop exercise for 2026-04-01
